content_voiceover: This slide shows the landmark long-term outcomes for dose-adjusted EPOCH-rituximab in Burkitt lymphoma from Dunleavy and colleagues, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2013. In HIV-negative patients treated with DA-EPOCH-R, at a median follow-up of eighty-six months, freedom from progression was ninety-five percent and overall survival was essentially one hundred percent. That's a remarkable result for such an aggressive lymphoma using a relatively lower-intensity, outpatient-friendly regimen compared to HyperCVAD-type approaches. Even more striking, in HIV-positive patients treated with the short-course variant, SC-EPOCH-RR, at a median follow-up of seventy-three months, freedom from progression was one hundred percent and overall survival was ninety-five percent. The Kaplan-Meier curves confirm durable, essentially flat survival plateaus in both cohorts. This data helped establish dose-adjusted EPOCH-R as a highly effective, less toxic alternative to intensive regimens like HyperCVAD or CODOX-M slash IVAC for Burkitt lymphoma, in both HIV-negative and HIV-positive populations.
keypoints: Dose-adjusted EPOCH-R gives durable cures with less toxicity than HyperCVAD-type regimens
keypoint_voiceover: Dose-adjusted EPOCH-rituximab produces excellent outcomes in Burkitt lymphoma, roughly ninety-five to one hundred percent freedom from progression and overall survival in both HIV-negative and HIV-positive patients, per Dunleavy's NEJM 2013 paper. This is a lower-intensity alternative to HyperCVAD that still cures nearly everyone.
